forbidden_actions: request, reveal, print, persist, hash, or transmit credential or secret values
perform source, local-system, browser, provider, publication, or remote mutations outside the exact atomic scope and fresh authorization
invent commands, exits, duration, artifacts, captures, provider receipts, benchmark results, approval, or completion evidence
combine independent evidence or findings with remediation, risk acceptance, publication, deployment, or release
claim evaluation, approval, release, or completion evidence that has not been produced
hard_gates: Pairing requires per-action authorization for exact agent, origins, actions, transport, exposure, and expiry; wildcard, hidden, reusable, or non-revocable credentials are blocked.
Independent review, QA, audit, acquisition, analysis, and triage never imply remediation; setup or authentication never implies downstream action authority.
Verification authority is read-only: it cannot mint or renew credentials, restart the daemon, change config, widen scope, or treat connectivity as data-access authorization.
Authentication setup grants neither page-data authority nor general browsing scope; credential values never enter prompts, logs, hashes, receipts, or artifacts.
Session configuration is ephemeral runtime state: it cannot persist credentials or system config, pair agents, authorize data access, or perform the browser task itself.
inputs: Running browser daemon, selected agent, local or remote mode, scope restrictions, credential retention, and explicit authorization.
Pairing identity, browser status, expected scope, target platform, and permitted external read boundary.
Browser profile, target origin, credential authority, local-system write authorization, retention, and deletion policy.
A validated browser task, session identifier, project path, wrapper contract, and CLI configuration.
permission_identity_is_default: most common of mode_permissions; the effective identity for a run is mode_permissions[selected_mode]
responsibility: Consolidated capability covering 4 related modes: Provision one scoped expiring browser-agent pairing identity after explicit local-system, credential, and network-exposure authorization, with revocation and cleanup.; Verify and diagnose an existing browser-agent pairing through approved local checks and read-only external observation without creating credentials or changing configuration.; Configure authorized authentication state in one local browser profile for exact origins without exposing values or granting unrelated browsing authority.; Create an isolated ephemeral browser runtime invocation from validated prerequisites without writing persistent auth, pairing, or project source.
